inputs.subject: Investor wants to put 20% in NVDA. Starting from the current portfolio, build a hypothetical allocation that preserves capital with some growth, low-moderate risk, 3-5 year horizon, no crypto, and includes NVDA at the highest weight that passes governance (if 20% does not pass, say so and give the maximum acceptable weight).

output.headline: A 20% NVDA position fails governance; the maximum acceptable NVDA weight is about 5%, and the verified proposal holds NVDA at 5% within a diversified, low-moderate-risk mix.

governance.evidence: Final proposal PASSes all checks (evidence ev-aae1dc8931): 2022 stress max loss -12.6% vs -15% limit; single position max 9.7% (RY.TO incl. ETF look-through); sector max 18.6% vs 35%; crypto 0%; SHORT_HORIZON_VOLATILITY at its 5% limit (exactly at threshold); SHORT_HORIZON_DEFENSIVE 43% vs 30%. The 20% NVDA version BLOCKED (ev-9de6c73e44): 2022 max loss -21.1% vs -15%, NVDA single position 20% vs 10%, and short-horizon volatility 20% vs 5%. The 8% NVDA version also BLOCKED on short-horizon volatility (8% vs 5%) and its stress max loss was -14.4% (ev-5173e5ad06).

details: 20% NVDA does not pass. Replacing 20% of the current portfolio with NVDA (scaling the rest pro rata) gives a 2022 stress loss of -21.1% against a -15% limit, so governance BLOCKs (ev-9de6c73e44).

max_position tool (ev-829a97a221) gives a stress-only ceiling of about 9% for NVDA. However, the short-horizon volatility rule caps NVDA at 5% for a 3–5 year horizon, which is the binding constraint. The 8% version still BLOCKs on that rule.
NVDA's 2022 total return was -46.9% (ev-c049970432), so its drawdown dominates the stress result. At 5% it adds about 2.3 pts of 2022 loss.

Defensive core: XBB.TO (30%) and ZST.TO (13%) are the bond and cash sleeves. XIU.TO (28%) provides broad Canadian equity. JNJ (8%) and RY.TO (7%) add diversification. RY.TO is trimmed to keep its look-through exposure under 10%. FTS.TO is trimmed to 9% to stay under the single-position limit.
Stress result for the final mix: 2022 return -7.0%, worst point -12.6% (about -$50.4k on $400k CAD), per ev-aae1dc8931 (illustrative only, not a forecast).
Growth is modest by design. The 5% NVDA sleeve is the only high-volatility holding. Raising NVDA further would need either a looser horizon rule or a higher loss tolerance from the investor.
Hypothetical allocation for scenario analysis, not investment advice.
